manifest.name: @andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review
manifest.description: Presents plan-review questions inline in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI composer: full plan markdown, highlight-to-comment, Accept/Request changes.

bundle.text:
# @andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review bundle: one client+host plugin row.
#
# The host half only serves workspace-confined plan files to the browser half
# (GET /plan-review/file?path=...). The client half claims pending
# ask_user_question requests whose header starts with `[plan-review]`.
#
# Optional row config (all defaults shown; every key is optional):
#   config:
#     maxPlanBytes: 2000000   # read cap for one plan file
- insert:
    - id: plan-review
      name: '@andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review'

readme.section: @andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review — read the whole plan before you approve it
readme.text:
An **unofficial community plugin** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
(DSH). Repository: <https://github.com/andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review>. It removes
one specific piece of friction in the superpowers workflow:

> The agent asks you to approve a plan. The question card shows
> `path: C:\ws\.superpowers\plans\feature.md` and two buttons — so you open the
> markdown file by hand just to find out what you are approving.

readme.section: @andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review — read the whole plan before you approve it
readme.text:
With this plugin installed, that question takes over the composer and renders
the **complete plan inline**, with `Accept plan` / `Revise plan` at the top and
**highlight → comment** on any passage. You decide with the plan on screen.

| property | behavior |
|---|---|
| trigger | an `ask_user_question` request whose single question header starts with `[plan-review]` |
| presentation | composer takeover: sticky decision header, full plan markdown, scrollable body, comment rail |
| plan source | `path: <absolute .md>` on the question's first line, read through the plugin's own host route; without a path, the question text itself is the plan |
| comments | select text in the plan → `Add comment`; each comment anchors to the quoted passage, is editable/deletable, and can be located again |
| accept | answers with the question's own accept label; refused while comments or an overall note exist, so feedback is never silently dropped |
| revise | sends `{decision, comments, note}` back in the answer's `custom` field; refuses locally when there is no feedback yet |
| drafts | comments and the overall note are kept in this browser tab's session storage, so closing and reopening the review does not lose them; answering clears the draft |
| fallback | unreadable plan or an unclaimed question shows the shipped card / an inline error; the review stays answerable |
| keyboard | `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` accepts; `Escape` clears a pend

- DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.2` with the Web GUI (`dsh web`).
- The superpowers workflow's `superpowers-ui` skill (installed under
  `$DSH_HOME/skills/`) emits the `[plan-review]` protocol this plugin renders.
- Node.js 22 or newer only for the tests and the client build; the plugin itself
  runs inside the harness process.

The package is a DSH **bundle**: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and one
client+host plugin row (`id: plan-review`). Install it into the profile you run,
then restart `dsh web`.

Enable DSH's custom plugin market, add a community index that lists this package
(the repository carries the **`dsh-plugin`** GitHub topic so indexes can discover
it), and install `@andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review` from the Discover tab.

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  target: @andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review@0.1.0
```

```
plugin_manager install_bundle  target: /absolute/path/to/dsh-plan-review
```

**Restart `dsh web`.** The running process holds its pre-install module graph; a
restart loads the new host half and the client bundle. Then confirm the
composition:

```
dsh --profile web --dump-config
```

Expected: exit code 0 and a row `id: plan-review` / `name: @andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review`
with no `not found`, `unknown key`, or `cannot resolve` lines.

- **Claim.** The plugin's client half registers into the `conversation.composer`
  chain slot at `priority: -20` — ahead of the shipped question composer (`0`),
  the approval panel (`1`) and the subagent read-only composer (`-10`). Its
  selector returns a claim only for a single generic question whose header
  starts with `[plan-review]`; every other interaction gets `null`, so the
  shipped card is untouched. (A question must carry at most two options and not
  be multi-select; anything else also falls back.)
- **Protocol.** The question text is `path: <absolute markdown file>` on line
  one, followed by the review heading. Without a `path:` line the whole text is
  the plan. The option labels are the authority for the decision buttons;
  accept-like and revise-like labels are matched by pattern and sent back
  verbatim.
- **Host half.** `GET /plan-review/file?path=…` (loopback-only, read-only) reads
  the plan as UTF-8. Reads are confined to the profile's registered workspace
  roots plus the sandbox policy's `workspaceRoot`; binary extensions, oversized
  files, and paths outside those roots are refused with stable error codes.
  `GET /plan-review/ping` is the liveness probe.

```json
{
  "id": "plan-review",
  "header": "[plan-review]",
  "question": "path: C:\\ws\\.superpowers\\plans\\feature.md\nReview the plan below.",

Answers arrive in the `ask_user_question` result. A plain decision is
`selected: ["Accept plan"]`. A comment-bearing decision instead has
`selected: []` and `custom` holding
`{"decision": "<label>", "comments": [{"quote": "<passage>", "note": "<what to change>"}], "note": "<overall note>"}`.
`note` is this plugin's additive field for an overall remark (the skill documents
`decision` + `comments`); a body that had to be shortened to fit one tool result
also carries `"truncated": true`. Locate each quoted passage in the plan file,
apply every note (never drop one), rewrite the plan, and ask again.

The plugin refuses to send an accept answer while comments or an overall note
exist: a label decision has no field for them, so it asks for
`Request changes` (or for the comments to be deleted) instead.

The plugin row accepts one optional value; it is read without a Config schema:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: plan-review
      name: '@andrewhmir/dsh-plan-review'
      config:

- **The `[plan-review]` protocol only.** The harness's native plan-mode review
  (`exit_plan_mode`, architect preset) is a separate, shipped surface and is
  deliberately not touched — this plugin exists to render superpowers plan files.
- **Plan files must live under a workspace root.** A plan outside every
  registered root is refused by design (the error names the path so it can be
  fixed). The route only serves markdown/text plan files (`.md`, `.markdown`,
  `.mdown`, `.mkd`, `.mdx`, `.txt`), never arbitrary workspace files.
- **Drafts are per browser tab.** Comments survive closing and reopening the
  review in the same tab (`sessionStorage`); they are not synced to another tab
  or device, and answering the review clears them.
- **Malformed answers are capped.** The encoded answer stays under the profile's
  tool-result pruner budget; if it had to shrink, the payload says
  `"truncated": true` so the agent can ask rather than silently missing notes.
- **English panel copy.** Package metadata is bilingual; in-panel strings are
  English in this version.
- **Web GUI only.** The host route is generic, but the takeover and comments are
  Web-client features.

`engines.dsh` declares `>=0.2.1-rc.2`. The composer chain, the question answer
wire schema, the loopback web route and the seeded React module were implemented
against the `0.2.1-rc.2` packages on this machine and are covered by a
unit/integration suite with fake React, fake storage and fake fetch (no live
browser is driven by the tests). Plan rendering is self-contained and does not
depend on the shell's markdown primitive. Live install + smoke-test evidence is
recorded in [`MOUNT.md`](MOUNT.md) once performed.

From this directory:

```
node --test "test/*.test.mjs"
node tools/build-client.mjs --check
node --check client.js
```

In a confined Windows sandbox the test runner's child-process spawn is blocked;
run `node --test --test-isolation=none "test/*.test.mjs"` there instead.

```
node tools/build-client.mjs         # regenerate client.js from src/client/*.mjs
node tools/build-client.mjs --check # fail when client.js is stale
node --test "test/*.test.mjs"
```

`client.js` is a generated classic script that registers itself with the
harness's module loader under the package name. Source modules under
`src/client/` are plain ESM with relative `.mjs` imports only; the host half
lives in `src/host/` and is injected with `webServer` (optional
`workspaceRegistry` / `sandboxPolicy`).

After editing only the client half, the harness's client HMR stat-polls the
built bundle and hot-swaps it in the open page. Host-half edits need a
`dsh web` restart.

This is an unofficial community plugin, not affiliated with DeepSeek. It is an
independent implementation of the inline plan-review idea for the superpowers
protocol; its predecessor on this machine was the private `dsh-superpowers-ui`
plugin (0.1.x API, retired in the 0.2.x upgrade). Upstream DSH does not accept
external pull requests at the moment, so distribution is a standalone package;
the repository carries the `dsh-plugin` topic so community plugin indexes can
discover it.
